title: B1 Grammar Quiz 2 — Third Conditional, Modal Perfect, Reported Commands

questions.question: If I ___ harder, I ___ the exam.
questions.explanation: Third Conditional (unreal past): If + Past Perfect, would have + past participle.

questions.question: She ___ the job if she ___ on time.
questions.explanation: Third Conditional: would have + pp in main clause, Past Perfect in if-clause.

questions.question: If he ___ so fast, he ___ the accident.
questions.explanation: Negative Third Conditional: 'hadn't + pp' in if-clause, 'wouldn't have + pp' in main clause.

questions.question: You ___ told me earlier! Now it's too late.
questions.explanation: 'Should have + pp' = regret or criticism about a past action that didn't happen.

questions.question: I ___ the bus. I'm late now. (miss — regret)
questions.explanation: 'Shouldn't have + pp' = it was a mistake to do something. Regret about an action that DID happen.

questions.question: She looks exhausted. She ___ worked all night.
questions.explanation: 'Must have + pp' = strong deduction about a past action (we are almost certain).

questions.question: He ___ taken your bag — he was with me all day.
questions.explanation: 'Can't have + pp' = strong negative deduction about the past (we are almost certain it didn't happen).

questions.question: I'm not sure why she's late. She ___ got stuck in traffic.
questions.explanation: 'Might have + pp' = weak deduction or possibility about the past (not certain).

questions.question: 'Sit down,' said the teacher. → The teacher told us ___.
questions.explanation: Reported commands: tell/ask + object + to-infinitive. 'told us to sit down'.

questions.question: 'Don't touch it,' she said. → She told me ___ it.
questions.explanation: Negative reported commands: 'told + object + not to + base verb'.

questions.question: 'Please help me,' she said. → She asked me ___.
questions.explanation: Reported requests with 'ask': ask + object + to-infinitive: 'asked me to help her'.

questions.question: I ___ my hair ___ at the salon.
questions.explanation: Causative: 'have/get + object + past participle'. Both 'had my hair cut' and 'got my hair cut' are correct.

questions.question: She ___ her car ___ last week.
questions.explanation: Causative past: 'had + object + past participle'. 'Service' → 'serviced'.

questions.question: The road ___ at the moment. That's why there are delays.
questions.explanation: Passive Present Continuous: 'is/are being + past participle'.

questions.question: She studies hard ___ pass the exam.
questions.explanation: 'In order to + base verb' expresses purpose. 'For' is followed by a noun. 'So that' is followed by a clause.

questions.question: He left early ___ he could avoid the traffic.
questions.explanation: 'So that + subject + could/would/can/will' expresses purpose with a full clause.

questions.question: I didn't study. I wish I ___ studied.
questions.explanation: 'Wish + Past Perfect' expresses regret about something that didn't happen in the past.

questions.question: I wish you ___ talk so loudly!
questions.explanation: 'Wish + would' expresses irritation about someone's habit or wish for them to change behaviour.

questions.question: The film ___ we saw last night was brilliant.
questions.explanation: In defining relative clauses, 'which/that' can be omitted when it is the object: 'The film (that) we saw'.

questions.question: I have ___ money left. I can't buy anything.
questions.explanation: 'Little' (without 'a') = almost none — negative connotation. 'A little' = some — positive connotation. 'Money' is uncountable.

questions.question: ___ students passed the test — only two out of thirty.
questions.explanation: 'Few' (without 'a') = almost none, negative. 'Students' is countable plural.

questions.question: When I was a child, I ___ climb trees.
questions.explanation: Both 'used to' and 'would' can describe past repeated actions. 'Used to' can also describe past states; 'would' cannot.

questions.question: She ___ live in France. (past state, no longer true)
questions.explanation: For past states → only 'used to' (not 'would'): 'used to live'. 'Would' is only for repeated actions.

questions.question: I'm not ___ driving on the left.
questions.explanation: 'Be used to + -ing/noun' = accustomed to something. It refers to present habit that is now familiar (or not).

questions.question: She is slowly ___ the cold weather.
questions.explanation: 'Get used to + -ing/noun' = the process of becoming accustomed to something.

questions.question: This form ___ by the manager.
questions.explanation: Passive with modal: 'modal + be + past participle': 'must be signed'.

questions.question: I ___ told you! Why didn't you listen?
questions.explanation: Emphatic 'did' stresses that the action really happened: 'I did tell you!' (past emphasis).

questions.question: ___ it was raining, we went for a walk.
questions.explanation: 'Although + clause' (subject + verb) expresses concession. 'Despite/In spite of' + noun/gerund.

questions.question: He ___ in the accident.
questions.explanation: Both 'got injured' (informal passive with get) and 'was injured' (formal passive) are correct.

questions.question: If she ___ the truth, she ___ him now.
questions.explanation: Mixed Conditional: past condition (3rd conditional if-clause) → present result (2nd conditional main clause).
